Notes: Turner Moore and Eliza Jones are parents, not identified enslavers. No plantation is named in the available transcription. Secondary UAH sources associate Eliza, Columbus, and Reuben with the Jones plantation west of Huntsville, now conventionally called Avalon. The exact legal enslaver of Columbus remains unconfirmed; do not convert this parentage record into a plantation-ownership claim. I found two Freedmen's Bureau labor contract (Employment) records for a Columbus Jones in Ancestry collection 62309: one dated 1867 (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/62309/records/2825623, image 007636376_00543) and one dated 16 Feb 1867 (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/62309/records/2827251, image 007636376_00658), both NARA Roll 15 "Fair Copies of Contracts Vol 3, Jan 1867-Jan 1868," Huntsville, Madison Co., AL. I think these bracket the Oct 1867 Freedmen's Savings Bank application nicely in time and place, which is encouraging corroboration -- but I haven't opened the actual contract images yet to check for explicit family language, so for now I'm treating this as circumstantial corroboration only, not confirmed proof it's the same Columbus Jones. UPDATE (2026-08-03, direct image review): I opened the actual contract image for record 2827251 (image 007636376_00658, columbus_jones_contract_feb1867_00658.jpg) directly rather than relying on the index. It IS a genuine Feb. 16, 1867 Madison County, AL contract, and it explicitly reads "...between Columbus Jones and brother Turner Jones of the second part..." -- this is now direct primary-source confirmation of a Columbus-Turner BROTHER relationship, upgraded from circumstantial to confirmed. Naming nuance I want to flag: this document says "Turner JONES," not "Turner Moore" (the surname in the Freedmen's Bank application above). I'm treating this as an open naming discrepancy, not a contradiction -- the same man could go by two names in different records. I also checked image 007636376_00543 (record 2825623) directly: it's actually a name-index ledger page reading "Jones, Columbus & bro," pointing to page 178 -- a citation/cross-reference for the contract above, not a second independent contract. Source: <https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/62309/records/2827251> (contract); <https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/62309/records/2825623> (index page). RESOLUTION (2026-08-03): I went back and looked closely at the image tied to this Turner Moore record (2821439, image 007636376_00370) and realized what happened. Donnell already documented elsewhere in this project.

[2026-09-04, 7.31.26 sweep] Corroborating citation found: 'The Avalon Plantation Marker Story' AHA/Auburn panel transcript (Nov. 10, 2020) refers to this same mother as 'Eliza Jones' (rather than 'Elizabeth') and states she and her three biracial children were manumitted in 1820 upon Lewellen Jones's death; panelists speculate (unproven) that the children's father was either Alexander Jones or Lewellen Jones. Treating 'Eliza' here as the same individual as 'Elizabeth' in this row pending further confirmation. Local file: The Avalon Plantation Marker Story_Transcript.pdf (uploaded to Avalon Key Findings Drive folder). [2026-09-24] The act read verbatim this pass: 'An Act to authorize John N. S. Jones and Alexander P. Jones to emancipate certain slaves therein named,' Acts Passed at the Second Session of the General Assembly of Alabama (Cahawba, 1820), approved Dec 11, 1820 (Internet Archive OCR) — a mulatto woman named Elizabeth, aged 40; a mulatto girl named Evelina, aged 13; a mulatto girl named Ann, aged 6; and a mulatto child named Shandy, 3 — on the single condition that the two Joneses post bond to the Madison County court chief justice, approved by the county court, securing that none of the four ever becomes chargeable to Alabama or any county or town therein. Legislative manumission, not self-purchase. The act states no kinship, names no father, gives no gender for Shandy, and gives no surnames. CORRECTION to the pending 'Eliza = Elizabeth' treatment above: do NOT merge — Elizabeth (b. ~1780, 40 in 1820) is not Eliza Jones, mother of Columbus (d. fall 1861 at her son's home); the age math makes the identification remote (Elizabeth would have been ~47 at Columbus's ~1827 birth, ~53 at Reuben's, ~63 at Turner's). Also do NOT merge with Elizabeth wf Jerry McCauley, the deceased Elizabeth Jones (both named in Columbus's 1867 bank account), or Elizabeth, 11, in Shandy's 1860 Tuscaloosa household (his daughter). Post-1820: no record found — absent from Boucher's 1830/1840/1850 Madison free-negro head lists. Parents unresolved; children's father unresolved; prior ownership within Lewellen Jones's estate is a strong lead (scholarship + timing — will recorded Apr 1820, act passed Dec 1820), not proven. SJR25 (2017) gives the emancipation as Dec 1, 1820 — one day off the act's printed Dec 11; flag, don't adopt.

Last Name: Enslaved person named in Lewellen Jones's 23 Sep 1805 deed of gift to his daughter Frances Ann Maria Jones (Bedford/Campbell County VA)

Evidence: Daughter of Lane Jones and Anne Barber (Henley family Bible via Cary 1897); married John Jones 1759. CORRECTION: the 1966 chart's 'John Jones, son of Lane' is an error — John was Lane's son-in-law, Frances's husband. Four converging records: 1761 York Co. special verdict (names Frances Barber Jones among Lane's children); 1763 Cumberland Co. deed ('John Jones and Frances Barber Jones, his wife, of Louisa County' among Lane's heirs); 1792 Bedford deed (Capt. John Jones and Frances Barber Jones selling 314 ac); Bedford chancery read pass (John Jones's widow 'Frances B. Jones').
Notes: Mother of Llewellyn Jones — this is the link that fixes the lineage. Do NOT merge with the Frances rows 102, 110, 1271, 1905 (different women).

Evidence: Styled 'Captain' (militia title; Rev War service unverified). Married Frances Barber Jones 1759 — son-in-law of Lane Jones, not son. 'Of Louisa County' 1763; Bedford Co., VA by the 1790s; d. intestate ~1796 leaving 'an estate both real and personal to a large amount.' 1792 deed with Frances sold 314 acres (Bedford Deed Bk T p. 97); 1789 receipt gave son-in-law Philip Burton £180 VA currency plus ten enslaved people as a daughter's marriage portion. Children per Bedford chancery read pass (6 cases, 1805–1841): Llewellyn, Charles D., Elizabeth (m. Jesse Anderson), Nancy T. (m. Nelson Dawson); a possible Burton daughter unresolved.
Notes: Father of Llewellyn Jones. Do NOT merge with any other John Jones row (96, 126, 134, 218, 1105, 1206, 1838, 1953 — all different men).

Evidence: Only son of Orlando Jones and Martha Macon; b. June 15, 1707, St. Peter's Parish, New Kent Co. (parish register via Cary 1897); m. 1727 Anne Barber, daughter of Maj. William Barber. Six children (Henley Bible; 1761 York verdict): Martha, Anne, Lane Jr., Rowland, Frances (Barber Jones, b. Jan 26, 1740), William. Wealth: inherited Tidewater estate; tobacco; the Barber marriage folded a magistrate/Burgess father-in-law and the Archer/Hubard kin network into the line.
Notes: Great-grandfather of Llewellyn Jones. Do NOT merge with the enslaved people bequeathed 'to Lane Jones' in Orlando's 1719 will (DB2 rows 1159–1167) — those are people he enslaved, not him.

Evidence: Son of Rev. Rowland Jones. Planter, tobacco shipper, landlord, Burgess for King William Co. (1714, 1715, 1718). Married Martha Macon Jan 31, 1703 (d. May 4, 1716; one son Lane, one daughter Frances who married Col. John Dandridge), then Mary Elizabeth Williams. Died June 12, 1719 at the Queen's Creek mansion; will proved Yorktown Nov 16, 1719. Wealth: tobacco cargo, plantations, a Williamsburg rental tenement, livestock, ~21 enslaved people; died heavily in debt (Williamsburg house ordered sold). Via tombstone, parish register, Burgess lists, Cary 1897.
Notes: Great-great-grandfather of Llewellyn Jones. Tobacco shipment is documented; ship ownership is not — keep the distinction. The enslaved people he bequeathed (DB2 rows 1158–1176) are separate entries.

Evidence: First rector of Bruton Parish, VA (1674–1688); b. 1644 Swinbrook, Oxfordshire; Merton College, Oxford (matric. Nov 11, 1663); d. Apr 23, 1688, aged 48 (tombstone, Bruton churchyard). Also a substantial planter: will Aug 15, 1687 (proved Dec 13, 1688, Yorktown) left son Robert a 400-ac Pomonkey Neck plantation, son William 200 ac on Chickahominy Swamp, daughter Anna Maria 6,000 lbs tobacco and silver, widow Anne the dwelling and plantation for life then to son Orlando — plus enslaved people. 'By no means dependent upon his ministerial salary' (Cary 1897).
Notes: The immigrant generation; father of Orlando Jones. Do NOT claim ship ownership or transatlantic slave trading for him — the documented mechanism is tobacco plantations worked by enslaved labor. Do not merge with his father Rowland Jones (1608–1685).

Evidence: Vicar of Wendover (1664) and Dorney (1667–1685), Buckinghamshire, England; B.A. Christ Church, Oxford, 1632; rector of Little Kimble 1661. Will dated Sept 1, 1665: a comfortable but modest clerical estate — books and manuscripts and £25 to son Rowland, £5 bequests to the other children. Via Cary 1897.
Notes: Father of Rev. Rowland Jones; the English root of the line. The Welsh-origin tradition in some compiled genealogies is unresolved — Cary documents an Oxfordshire/Buckinghamshire clerical family and says nothing of Wales.

Evidence: Wife of Turner Moore and mother of Columbus Jones per Fred C. Rathbun's extraction of Columbus Jones's Freedman's Bank account 29 (M816 Roll 1, acct. 29, 2 Oct 1867); died fall 1861 at her son's home. Columbus, Turner, and Reuben carried her Jones surname. See DB1 rows 1718–1737 (Rathbun fold).
Notes: HYPOTHESIS ONLY — unproven, do not treat as fact: if Eliza was enslaved by the Jones family while Turner was held by a Moore, the family could have formed across two neighboring plantations — the "abroad marriage" pattern — with the children carrying the mother's Jones surname. The 1860 slave schedule puts Alexander P. Jones (96 enslaved, stamped pp. 483–484) adjacent to Benj. T. Moore (stamped 487–488) in the NW Division. Forced separation by sale is unsupported; the mechanism is unknown. Do not merge Eliza with any enslaver's holding without direct evidence.
